request.system: You are an expert in clinical classification systems.

messages.content:
ICD-10-AM is the Australian modification of the International Statistical Classification of Diseases and Related Health Problems, 10th revision. Its disease codes are arranged in chapters, and a three-character category is written as one capital letter followed by two digits. The letter indicates the chapter or block: A and B are infectious diseases, C is malignant neoplasms, D is other neoplasms and blood disorders, E is endocrine, nutritional and metabolic disease, F is mental and behavioural disorders, G is the nervous system, H is the eye and ear, I is the circulatory system, J is the respiratory system, K is the digestive system, L is the skin, M is the musculoskeletal system, N is the genitourinary system, O is pregnancy and childbirth, P is the perinatal period, Q is congenital malformations, R is symptoms and abnormal findings, S and T are injury and poisoning, and Z is factors influencing health status. The two digits narrow the chapter to a specific category, for example J44 is chronic obstructive pulmonary disease and N17 is acute kidney failure.

The principal diagnosis is the single condition established after investigation to be chiefly responsible for the patient's episode of admitted care. It is not the patient's most serious comorbidity, not the presenting symptom, and not the procedure performed.

Using that structure, assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category for the episode below. Choose the chapter letter first, then the two digits.

Hospital course:
Hospital Course:
The patient presented with altered mental status, visual disturbances, and seizures associated with a rash and polyarthralgia. She was found to have hypertension and polysubstance abuse. Antinuclear antibodies (ANA) and double-stranded deoxyribonuclease (dsDNA) antibodies were both positive, and C3 and C4 complement factors were low. The patient was diagnosed with SLE and started on methylprednisolone pulse therapy due to active proliferative lupus nephritis. Her kidney function and arthralgia improved, and she was transitioned to oral prednisone taper. Mycophenolate mofetil was also started, and pneumocystis pneumonia (PCP) prophylaxis was given. The patient's hospital stay was significant for treatment of SLE related manifestations and hypertension. 
Discharge Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Disposition:
The patient was discharged home with close follow-up with her primary care physician and rheumatologist for continuation of management of her SLE and hypertension. 

Instructions:
The patient is advised to continue medications as prescribed and report any adverse effects to her physician. She should monitor her blood pressure and follow a low-sodium diet. She should avoid sun exposure and use sunscreen for protection. The patient is to have close follow-up with her physician for monitoring of her kidney function and disease activity. 

Follow-Up:
Urgent follow-up is recommended with the primary care physician and rheumatologist within one week.

Answer in the form CODE: <letter><digit><digit>

text:
CODE: M32

The principal diagnosis is systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), which falls under category M32 in the musculoskeletal and connective tissue chapter. The admission was for SLE with active proliferative lupus nephritis, and the treatment was directed at these manifestations. Hypertension and polysubstance abuse were comorbidities and do not change the principal diagnosis.
